title: Ich kann, ich muss, ich will
summary: The modal verbs können/wollen/müssen/dürfen/möchten and the rule that sends the infinitive to the end of the sentence

blocks.title: Fünf kleine Wörter, viel Macht
blocks.body: Modal verbs frame what you *can, want to, have to, are allowed to,* or *would like to* do. They conjugate like normal verbs, but they always send the **main verb** to the **infinitive**, parked at the very **end** of the sentence: **Ich möchte einen Kaffee bestellen.** The modal takes the normal V2 spot; the infinitive waits at the end.

rows: ich kann, du kannst, er kann
ich will, du willst, er will
ich muss, du musst, er muss
ich darf, du darfst, er darf
ich möchte, du möchtest, er möchte

blocks.callout: *möchten* is the polite cousin of *wollen* — always the safer choice when ordering or asking.

blocks.title: Die Satzklammer: Modal … Infinitiv
blocks.body: Picture the sentence as a bracket: the **modal verb** clicks into position two, and the **infinitive** rides at the very end, no matter how much sits in between. *Ich* **muss** *heute noch zwei Brötchen für das Abendbrot* **kaufen.** The bracket holds everything else inside it.
blocks.callout: One new thing: the infinitive always goes LAST — even in a long sentence.

pairs.left: Du musst nicht kommen. — you don't HAVE to come (it's optional)
pairs.right: Du darfst hier nicht rauchen. — you're NOT ALLOWED to smoke here (it's forbidden)
pairs.note: The classic trap: *nicht müssen* removes an obligation; *nicht dürfen* is a flat-out ban.

blocks.prompt: 'You are not allowed to park here.' — which modal fits?
blocks.explain: *dürfen* + *nicht* = forbidden. *musst nicht* would mean it's simply optional, not banned.

blocks.prompt: Type: 'I would like to order a bread roll.' (use möchten)
blocks.explain: *Ich möchte ein Brötchen bestellen.* — *möchte* in position two, *bestellen* waits at the end.

blocks.title: Bau deinen Modalsatz
blocks.prompt: Build a sentence: subject + modal, then an object, then the infinitive at the end.

lines.en: I still have to go shopping.

blocks.prompt: Write three sentences about today using three different modal verbs — one thing you can do, one you must do, and one you'd like to do.
